name: Centro Cultural de la República El Cabildo
funding: Cultural arm of Paraguay's National Congress, paid from the congressional budget (a G. 1.88 billion extension for a new building in 2025). Entry to the ground-floor rooms is free.
watch: Shows mid-20th-century to present Paraguayan art, including Olga Blinder and Livio Abramo. A December 2020 fire hit the newer block; the heritage building was safe.
records_note: Its site has programme and news pages only; no reports, accounts, funders or board are posted, and its parent is the Paraguayan Congress.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Santo Domingo
funding: State museum run by the Dominican Ministry of Culture on the Plaza de la Cultura; its director sits on the ministry's Bienal Nacional commission.
watch: After a December 2019 protest, artists' open letters in 2020 and 2021 blamed the ministry, the museum and its directors for the Bienal's delays.
why_flagged: State museum run by the Dominican Ministry of Culture on the Plaza de la Cultura; its director sits on the ministry's Bienal Nacional commission.
records_note: It posts nothing itself; its parent Ministry of Culture posts annual memorias for 2016 to 2025 and financial statements for 2020 to 2025.

name: Festival Internacional Cervantino
funding: 2023 budget 168.8M pesos: federal culture ministry 65.3M, Guanajuato 36M, guest country and state 42M, embassies 10.2M, sponsors 15.4M. Sponsors include Yamaha, Mazda, Megacable, HONOR and the FEMSA group.
watch: Name to know: Coca-Cola FEMSA, a named sponsor. Chiapas groups have sought to revoke its water permit since 2017; no campaign targets the festival.
why_flagged: Name to know: Coca-Cola FEMSA, a named sponsor. Chiapas groups have sought to revoke its water permit since 2017; no campaign targets the festival.
records_note: Names sponsors on a 2025 edition page and lists its government hosts and programming committee; no annual reports or audited accounts exist online.

name: Espacio Cultural Patiño
funding: Financed by the Patiño foundations: the Bolivian university foundation Simón I. Patiño created in 1931 and the Geneva foundation his heirs set up in 1958.
watch: Opened 1984; one of three Patiño centres. La Paz bought two neighbouring houses and opened new galleries in 2018; over 35,000 visitors a year.
records_note: No records of its own; the Geneva Fundación Patiño posts activity reports 2022 to 2025 and names its board, with no accounts or donor list.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Caracas
funding: Venezuelan public museum, under the state's Fundación Museos Nacionales since 2005, with the Ministry of Culture overseeing it.
watch: Chávez dismissed founder Sofía Ímber on air in January 2001. A January 2006 Culture Ministry notice dropped her name from the museum.
why_flagged: Venezuelan public museum, under the state's Fundación Museos Nacionales since 2005, with the Ministry of Culture overseeing it. No private sponsor found.
records_note: The museum's site and its parent foundation's site did not load, so its records are unchecked.

name: Mémorial ACTe
funding: Public cultural body since 2019 joining the French state, Région Guadeloupe, the Département, Cap Excellence and Pointe-à-Pitre. The Région's then-president launched the €83M building.
watch: The regional audit court found serious irregularities in 2023. In April 2024 the financial prosecutor searched the Région's offices over the Mémorial's contracts.
why_flagged: The regional audit court found serious irregularities in 2023. In April 2024 the financial prosecutor searched the Région's offices over the Mémorial's contracts.
records_note: Its site carries ticketing, collections and administrative notices only; no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board are published.

name: Gallerie d'Italia
funding: Owned and funded by Intesa Sanpaolo through its Progetto Cultura. Four museums in Milan, Naples, Turin and Vicenza drew over 750,000 visitors in 2024. No museum budget is published.
watch: About 30 Extinction Rebellion activists occupied the Turin site on 2 March 2025 over owner Intesa Sanpaolo's investments. One institution, four sites.
why_flagged: Owned and funded by Intesa Sanpaolo through its Progetto Cultura. Four museums in Milan, Naples, Turin and Vicenza drew over 750,000 visitors in 2024. No museum budget is published.
records_note: It posts nothing itself; owner Intesa Sanpaolo posts annual reports and accounts for 2007 to 2025 and names its board, with no donor list.

name: Fondazione Palazzo Strozzi
funding: 2025 income EUR 11.7M. Fondazione CR Firenze gave 1.1M, the Partners Committee 928k, the Recordati foundation 600k, Intesa Sanpaolo 464k. City, Region and Metropolitan City gave 500k each.
watch: Enegan, a Florence retailer of gas and power, is a Partner and has supplied the Fondazione's renewable electricity since 2021. Visitors in 2025: 384,176.
why_flagged: 2025 income EUR 11.7M. Fondazione CR Firenze gave 1.1M, the Partners Committee 928k, the Recordati foundation 600k, Intesa Sanpaolo 464k. City, Region and Metropolitan City gave 500k each.
records_note: Reports run from 2007 to 2025, accounts with a KPMG audit are posted, the 2025 report names funders with amounts, and the board is listed.

name: Palazzo Grassi and Punta della Dogana
funding: Private. Pinault bought Palazzo Grassi in 2005 (EUR 29M). The City of Venice owns Punta della Dogana; he holds it on a 33-year agreement and paid its EUR 20M restoration.
watch: Bottega Veneta, a Kering house, solely backs the 2026 Lorna Simpson show. Kering paid EUR 1.25bn in 2019 to settle an Italian tax case.
why_flagged: Bottega Veneta, a Kering house, solely backs the 2026 Lorna Simpson show. Kering paid EUR 1.25bn in 2019 to settle an Italian tax case.
records_note: The site lists staff led by François Pinault and the managing director; it posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Triennale Milano
funding: 2022 revenue EUR 11.4M: Ministry of Culture 2.9M, other public grants 5.3M, tickets 2.1M. Eni was an institutional partner and Main Partner of the 23rd Exhibition, with Lavazza.
watch: 661,234 visitors in 2022. Eni was also Main Sponsor of Progetto Genesi at Triennale in 2023, run by Associazione Genesi.
why_flagged: 2022 revenue EUR 11.4M: Ministry of Culture 2.9M, other public grants 5.3M, tickets 2.1M. Eni was an institutional partner and Main Partner of the 23rd Exhibition, with Lavazza.
records_note: Its site blocked fetches; search listings show reports and accounts for 2006 to 2025, partners named without a date, and a named board.

name: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea
funding: Ministry of Culture state museum. The ministry paid EUR 1.5M for its 2024-25 Futurism show. Main sponsors were Autostrade per l'Italia and Enel; Ferrovie dello Stato and Unipol also sponsored.
watch: Enel made 82% of its 2025 power emission-free but runs gas plants. Autostrade per l'Italia held the Genoa bridge concession when it fell in 2018.
why_flagged: Enel made 82% of its 2025 power emission-free but runs gas plants. Autostrade per l'Italia held the Genoa bridge concession when it fell in 2018.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2015 to 2023, a transparency portal with budgets and final accounts, and its board and auditors; no standing sponsor list.

name: Centro Botín
funding: Run by Fundación Botín. Patrons: Fundación Mutua Madrileña, Fundación Prosegur, Roche España and two public tourism bodies. Strategic sponsors: Fundación EDP, Plenitude (Eni) and CESINE.
watch: Plenitude, controlled by Eni, sells gas and power in Spain from Santander. Fundación EDP is also a strategic sponsor. No protest found.
why_flagged: Run by Fundación Botín. Patrons: Fundación Mutua Madrileña, Fundación Prosegur, Roche España and two public tourism bodies. Strategic sponsors: Fundación EDP, Plenitude (Eni) and CESINE.
records_note: Fundación Botín posts annual reports from 2007 to 2025 and its trustees; the Centro Botín sponsor page names patrons and sponsors, undated.
